abi.pointer_models_note: How a function without a body treats pointers, for the points-to analysis (README, 'Library pointer models'). First match wins. The default, for anything not listed, is escape: every pointer argument escapes (library code may keep it and write anything through it, at any time), the result is a library pointer (EXT). Every entry weaker than that carries a note: the one line of the function's documented contract it rests on. Kinds: none (keeps no pointer, returns no pointer: a pointer result is EXT, an integer result has no provenance); fresh; realloc; ret_arg0/ret_arg1 (a pointer into that argument); copy (bytes of argument 1 into argument 0); data (container internals: size, reads, writes, closure, write_reached, self, bodies); ret_ext; throw; catch. Effects added to any kind: writes_bytes (the objects these arguments point to receive bytes from outside or computed bytes: they hold no provenance; an entry is an index, 'varargs', or {arg, size}); exposes (the address is revealed, as by %p); sends (the pointers stored in those bytes leave the process and may come back: their objects are exposed); permutes (pointers move within the object); calls (callbacks: fn called with args); format (printf-like: a constant format without %n/%p limits the varargs effects); va_list; fill_value (memset: a constant 0 writes nothing); fresh_unknown (mmap).

abi.intrinsic_inline_note: x86-64: a memcpy/memmove/memset of constant length up to 32 bytes is expanded into at most four 8-byte moves (below every target's MaxStoresPerMemcpy), never a library call
abi.intrinsics_no_call_note: Intrinsics that code generation never turns into a call (reviewed against LLVM 21's lowering for x86-64). Removed in round 5: trap/ubsantrap/debugtrap (they stop the process: abort class), instrprof.value.profile (calls __llvm_profile_instrument_target), instrprof.callsite (calls the contextual-profiling runtime). Lowered to calls by abi.intrinsic_libcalls instead: memcpy/memmove/memset above 32 constant bytes, libm intrinsics, powi, clear_cache, smul.with.overflow.i128 (__muloti4), convert.to/from.fp16 without F16C. Kept with a reason: threadlocal.address (the access itself is classified by the tls-dynamic rule), sadd/uadd/ssub/usub/umul.with.overflow and the bit operations (inline at every width), masked/vector operations (scalarized inline), x86.* except x86.int (machine instructions; llvm.x86.int is a software interrupt, syscall class).
abi.attr_libcalls_note: Rule (d). Function attributes that make code generation add a call. Each call is classified like a library call: the classes its summary gives, and external-unknown without one. Reviewed against Clang/LLVM 21 for x86-64: stack protector (ssp*), -finstrument-functions (instrument-function-*; -pg is instrument-function-entry-inlined=mcount), -mfentry (fentry-call), XRay (function-instrument, xray-instruction-threshold), -fpatchable-function-entry, stack probes through a named function (probe-stack; inline-asm probing calls nothing), split stacks (__morestack), SafeStack, external return thunks (fn_ret_thunk_extern) and external retpoline thunks (target feature). Sanitizer, coverage and profile instrumentation is inserted by IR passes before the bitcode is written: its calls are in the IR. shadowcallstack adds no call (register operations).
abi.asm_harmless_note: Rule (e). Inline assembly blocks that are known not to enter the kernel and not to transfer control, compared as exact strings after whitespace is normalised. The empty block is the optimisation barrier (asm volatile("" : : "r"(p) : "memory")). Every other block is an unknown callee.
abi.known_fn_attrs_note: Rule (d). String function attributes known not to add a call at code generation (floating-point modes, target selection, frame layout, diagnostics, profile data). A string attribute that is neither here nor in attr_libcalls is reported in module.unknown_function_attributes. Enumerated attributes are a closed set of LLVM 21; those that add a call are in attr_libcalls.
abi.known_module_flags_note: Rule (d). Module flags known not to add a call the IR does not show. Any other flag (Cross-DSO CFI, kcfi, ...) is reported in module.unknown_module_flags. -femulated-tls is not recorded in the IR at all: the driver passes it on when it sees the flag, and --emulated-tls says so for bare bitcode.

assumptions: The program has no undefined behaviour (in particular, no call through a function pointer of the wrong type, no out-of-bounds vtable use).

Whole program: the linked module contains every translation unit that defines a class with virtual functions used by the entries, and every address-taken function the entries can call through a pointer. Function pointers created inside libraries without bitcode are not seen.
ODR: linkonce_odr, weak_odr and available_externally bodies are the bodies the program runs.

No symbol interposition at run time (LD_PRELOAD, kernel-bypass libraries that replace socket calls, symbol versioning tricks): a call goes to the definition in the module or to the library named by the summary.

External functions call back only the functions passed to them as arguments (callback edges); callbacks stored by a library and called later are not modelled except through summaries with unresolved indirect calls.
Signal handlers and other threads are not part of an entry's call tree.

Analysis is of pre-link LTO bitcode at the optimisation level given; the final link-time optimisation can only remove calls, inline, or turn equivalent library calls into one another (for example malloc+memset into calloc).
Hand-written assembly files and inline assembly that does not match a policy pattern are not analysed.

resolution.note: exact: targets of a call through a function pointer are the address-taken functions of the same IR function type; arity: same number of parameters; any: every address-taken function
